newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign exchange rise due to capital account.
newsitem.headline: China foreign exchange rise due to capital account.

text.p: Investment income under the capital account has been the major contributor to China's rapidly expanding foreign exchange reserves, the China Securities Daily said on Monday.
China's foreign exchange reserves stood at a record $90.8 billion as of July and were expected to climb to nearly $100 billion by the end of this year.
The newspaper also quoted Zhou Xiaochuan, head of the State Administration of Exchange Control, as saying China would make gradual adjustments to its supervision of capital account items.
He said there was a need to ensure that purchases made under the capital account had proper approvals and was not used for current account items.
He also said there was a need to control foreign debt but gave no details of any new measures to tighten supervision.
